notes.meaning: Long after the royal line of King David seemed cut down like a fallen tree, a fresh green branch will sprout from its stump. This promised ruler comes from the family of Jesse, David's father, pointing to Christ's humble earthly beginnings. God can bring glorious new life out of what looks dead and forgotten.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that naming Jesse rather than David suggests a fresh beginning—a brand-new David—rather than simply another king in the royal line.

notes.meaning: God's Holy Spirit will rest on this King permanently, not just for a short time. The Spirit equips Him with perfect wisdom, practical guidance, mighty strength, and a heart devoted to the Lord. Because Christ was filled with the Spirit, He is able to supply His people with all the help they need.

differ.view: Reformed interpreters emphasize that this describes Christ's human nature receiving six distinct gifts of the Spirit, which He now shares with His church.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition finds seven gifts of the Holy Spirit here, counting piety (or godliness) from ancient Greek and Latin translations.

notes.meaning: The coming King finds His greatest delight in reverent obedience to the Lord. Human judges can be easily tricked by good looks or clever rumors, but He sees straight into every human heart. We can trust Him completely because His decisions are based on truth rather than outward shows.

This King stands up for the poor and protects the gentle who have no power of their own. His words carry such divine power that merely speaking judgment will strike down evil and ruin the wicked. Christ wins His victories not through earthly swords, but through the mighty power of His word.

Righteousness—doing what is completely right—and faithfulness wrap around the Messiah like a strong belt around a warrior's waist. A belt held clothes in place and showed a ruler was ready for action. Everything Christ does is held together by His perfect justice and His loyalty to His promises.

Fierce wild beasts and gentle farm animals will live together in complete peace, safely led by a young child. Poisonous snakes will lose their venom, so that toddlers can play near their nests without any harm. The rule of the Prince of Peace puts an end to all fear, cruelty, and violence.

differ.view: Many believe these words describe a literal physical change in nature that will take place during Christ's future thousand-year reign on earth.
Many see this as a word picture of the gospel changing cruel people into gentle believers, pointing forward to the final new earth.

notes.meaning: No harm or destruction will exist anywhere on God's holy mountain, which represents His church and kingdom. This lasting peace comes because true knowledge of the Lord will fill the earth just as deeply and completely as water fills the sea. When people truly know God's love, their desire to hurt one another disappears.

The Messiah will stand high like a royal army flag, drawing the attention of all humanity. People from non-Jewish nations will seek Him out for salvation, and the place where He dwells will be filled with divine glory. God's plan of grace reaches far beyond one nation to welcome people from every background.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translated 'his rest' as 'his sepulchre,' which led early Catholic commentators to view this as a prophecy of the glory of Christ's burial and tomb.

notes.meaning: The Lord will reach out His mighty hand a second time to rescue the remnant, which means the small surviving group of His scattered people. Just as He once brought Israel out of Egypt, He will bring His people back from world powers near and far. No matter where God's children are scattered, His loving power can bring them home.

differ.view: Many believe this foretells a future physical return of the Jewish people from all over the world to their homeland in the end times.
Many understand this as a spiritual gathering through the preaching of the gospel, uniting both scattered Jews and Gentiles into Christ's church.

notes.meaning: God will lift up the Messiah like a banner for all nations to see, calling the exiles of Israel and Judah home from every corner of the earth. The words include both men and women who were cast out and scattered abroad. Christ Himself is the standard around which all of God's wandering people are gathered.

The bitter rivalry between the northern tribes, called Ephraim, and the southern tribe of Judah will finally come to an end. They will no longer envy or trouble one another, and their shared enemies will be removed. God's grace heals deep family hurts and unites His people in genuine love.

United as one family, God's people will swoop down like birds of prey to defeat their hostile neighbors on every side. In the spiritual kingdom of the Messiah, this pictures the gospel winning victories over every opposing power. When believers stand together in unity, they share in Christ's triumph over evil.

The Lord will clear away massive natural barriers, drying up the gulf of the Red Sea and splitting the mighty Euphrates River into seven shallow streams. He will make it so easy to cross that His returning people will not even need to take off their sandals. No obstacle in the world can stop God when it is His time to deliver His people.

God will build a wide, open highway for the remnant returning from Assyria, just as He made a dry path through the sea when Israel left Egypt. The great miracles of the past show us what God can do whenever His people need rescue. When the Lord leads His children forward, He always makes a way.
